Cybertruck and Model X charging strategy replay

Real ComEd prices, 2025-04-02–2026-10-14. All six vehicle/mileage profiles charge at 11.5 kW, 20:00–07:00, 90% efficiency, with a 30-minute soft buffer. 554 usable nights per profile; seven skipped. Annualized averages assume daily charging.

Cybertruck retains the existing study assumption of 0.4 battery kWh/mile (44.44 wall-kWh/100 miles at 90% efficiency), not an EPA consumption claim. Its modeled capacity is 123 kWh; Tesla's battery rating does not distinguish gross and usable capacity. Model X is a 2025 Plaid on 22-inch wheels, using EPA 38 wall-kWh/100 miles and an assumed 95 kWh usable capacity. Capacity assumptions do not determine these nightly energy targets.

Every strategy delivered the requested energy on every retained night. Hindsight is an unattainable reference. Timer comparisons cover the six starts shown, not every possible timer. Capacity-charge dollars, household consumption and battery wear are excluded.

The browser replay contains no multi-night battery-buffer strategy; existing buffer research is separate.

Suggested nights: An ordinary night (2025-04-20); Negative-price hours (2026-01-26); A posted price spike (2025-04-07); January cold snap (2026-01-23).
